newsitem.title: USA: EchoStar debt soars, over $1 bln high-grades sold.
newsitem.headline: EchoStar debt soars, over $1 bln high-grades sold.

text.p: U.S. high-yield dealers watched the debt of EchoStar Communications Corp rise into high-orbit on Tuesday following news of a major investment by News Corp, traders said.
Meanwhile, investment grade issuers injected their market more than $1.0 billion in supply.
EchoStar's 13-1/8 percent zero coupon bonds due 2004 rose more than 10 points in early trade to an 83 bid, although trading in the name was quiet at the start.

Follow through buying in other satellite paper was enjoyed by holders of Globalstar and TCI Satellite bonds. TCI bonds faded as the day wore on, however, perhaps due to its vulnerable position next to the News Corp/EchoStar pact, according to high-yield analysts.
Late on Monday, News Corp said it would buy 50 percent of EchoStar in a deal valued at $1.0 billion. EchoStar stock on Tuesday jumped $8.75 to $26.75 on Nasdaq market.
Elsewhere, Penn Traffic Co debt gained for the third consecutive session but settled well off its highs.
Rumors of an imminent CEO hire and departure of current chairman Gary Hirsch sent bonds higher, traders said. Hirsch has been acting as CEO since the retirement of John Dixon on September 30.
Penn Traffic 9-5/8s traded at a high of 54 bid and closed up 1-1/4 points at 47-1/2 bid, 47-3/4 offer.
In ratings news, Moody's Investors Service cut Apple Computer Inc's senior unsecured debt rating to B3 from B1 and its subordinated debt to Caa from B3.
Traders appeared non-plussed by the double-notch downgrade and Apple debt was unchanged on the day.

Finally, Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's parent company bondholders were granted in U.S. bankruptcy court the right to vote to foreclose on the stock that collateralizes their debt. Judge Helen Balick ruled to remove an automatic stay that was triggered when Marvel Entertainment Group and its holding company's filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on December 27.
Markets for Marvel's "old" and "new" bonds were not seen late on Tuesday.

New junk issues were topped by $160 million 11-3/4 percent 10-year 144A senior notes from Dobson Communications Corp via lead manager Morgan Stanley & Co Inc. The notes were priced at par to yield 539 basis points over the Treasury curve.
In the high-grade arena, Salomon Inc increased its three-year Baa1/BBB note deal from $500 million to $750 million before pricing the bonds as 6-1/2s to yield 50 basis points over the curve.
Caterpillar Inc issued $300 million A2/single-A century bonds as 7-3/8s to yield 75 basis points over the T-bond via lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
Southwest Airlines Co sold $100 million A3/A-minus 30-year debentures as 7-3/8s to yield 70 basis points over.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged.
